1.why: The system checks that the reset code belongs to the user by validating the token against the session-bound reset record.

2.why: The reset code is session-specific and cannot work for other users due to session isolation.

3.why: Previous sessions are invalidated after password reset (reset.used = true clears the reset flow).

4.why: The service enforces HTTPS with TLS (mkcert certs) and redirects HTTP to HTTPS.

5.why: Reset codes are generated using crypto.randomBytes and encrypted in transit via HTTPS.

6.why: Email messages (simulated) do not expose private data; tokens are only shown in logs for testing.

7.why: User-supplied data (email, passwords) is normalized/sanitized (e.g., normalizeEmail, validPassword).

8.why: Redirect links are hardcoded to the hospital’s site (e.g., /recovery, /login) with no user-controlled URLs.

9.why: Email templates are static (no user input in HTML/scripts); logs only show simulated tokens.

10.why: Error pages/logs explicitly avoid exposing private info (e.g., 'no private account detail logged').

11.why: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt; no secrets are hardcoded (only a precomputed hash exists).

12.why: No default credentials are present; demo account requires recovery flow to set a password.

13.why: Throttling is implemented via isAllowed/failure (max attempts, lockout periods).

14.why: The system gives the same generic response for all email inputs, hiding account existence.

15.why: Reset codes are random (token(32)), complex (base64url), and user-specific (bound to accountId).
